newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Top clergyman calls for prayers to save Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Top clergyman calls for prayers to save Nigeria.

text.p: The Anglican Archibishop of Nigeria, Reverend Abiodun Adetiloye, on Thursday called for prayers to help his country solve its problems.

"The special prayers have become our bounden duty at a time such as we are in Nigeria today where nothing seems to work," Adetiloye said in a open letter to Nigerians titled "Prayer for a nation in crisis."

The leader of the Anglican communion, which has a sizeable following in southern Nigeria, wrote similar open letters in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential election and plunged Africa's most populous nation into turmoil.
His latest letter follows a five-week-long fuel shortage that has caused severe hardship for people in Nigeria, the world's sixth leading crude oil producer.
The military government of General Sani Abacha was earlier this week forced to resort to massive importation of oil products to end the fuel shortage.
Adetiloye in his letter asked Christians and non-Christians to "engage ourselves in fervent prayer every three hours around the clock.
"I suggest that all church leaders and anybody who feels like should pray these prayers prostrating as a sign of humility before the divine majesty of the Almighty God."

Nigeria is Africa's most populous nation with huge natural resources but is mired in economic and political problems and has been ruled by the military for 27 out of its 37 years of independence from Britain.
